items.name: Bessel connection and Kloosterman D-module of rank n
items.statement: Over a field K of characteristic 0 and λ ∈ K, the Bessel connection Be_n is the trivial rank-n bundle on G_{m,K} with ∇ = d + M(x) dx/x, where M(x) has 1 on the superdiagonal, λ^n x in the lower-left corner and 0 elsewhere; it is the system of the Bessel equation (x d/dx)^n f − λ^n x f = 0, whose solution holomorphic at 0 is Σ_{r≥0} (λ^n x)^r/(r!)^n. With add, mult : G_m^n → A¹, G_m and the exponential D-module E_λ, the Kloosterman D-module is Kl_n^dR = R^{n−1}mult_!(add^*E_λ); with E_λ = K⟨x, ∂_x⟩/(∂_x − λ) = (O, d + λ dx), the convention of §4.1.13, Be_n ≅ Kl_n^dR (the introduction's E_λ = (O, d − λ dx) changes Kl_n^dR by x ↦ (−1)^n x). Be_n is regular singular at 0 with unipotent monodromy of one Jordan block and irregular at ∞ with irregularity 1.
items.note: Sign conventions as in sourceIssues E22. The GL_n case of the Frenkel–Gross and Heinloth–Ngô–Yun constructions. The Kloosterman connection, its hypergeometric operator and its local structure are planned by the pending KloostermanMomentsAndPotentialAutomorphy proposal (PAPER-FRESAN-SABBAH-YU-22), which this item joins.

items.name: Kloosterman sums and Deligne's Kloosterman sheaf
items.statement: For a ∈ F_q^×, Kl(n; a) = (−1/√q)^{n−1} Σ_{z_i ∈ F_q^×} ψ(Tr_{F_q/F_p}(z_1 + ⋯ + z_{n−1} + a/(z_1⋯z_{n−1}))). With the Artin–Schreier sheaf AS_ψ, Deligne's Kl_n = Rmult_!(add^*AS_ψ)[n−1]((n−1)/2) on G_{m,F_p} satisfies: (i) its Frobenius trace at a ∈ F_q^× is Kl(n; a); (ii) it is an irreducible lisse sheaf of rank n, pure of weight 0, in degree 0, so |Kl(n; a)| ≤ n; (iii) it is tame at 0 with unipotent monodromy of one Jordan block; (iv) it is wild at ∞ with Swan conductor 1.
items.note: The normalisation differs from the usual sum by (−1/√q)^{n−1}. The pending KloostermanMomentsAndPotentialAutomorphy proposal plans Deligne's Kloosterman sheaf and its local invariants; FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums FF.2 plans the Weil bound only as a target of curve-based estimates.

items.name: Katz's monodromy groups of Kloosterman sheaves
items.statement: G_geo(Kl_n) = G_arith(Kl_n) is Sp_n for n even, SL_n for pn odd, SO_n for p = 2 and n odd with n ≠ 7, and G_2 for p = 2 and n = 7.
items.locator: §1.1.2, (1.1.2.3), p. 3 (Katz, Gauss sums, Kloosterman sums and monodromy groups, §11)
items.note: Recalled from Katz. The paper reproves it by the p-adic method (Theorem 4.5.2 with Corollary 4.5.6, and the appendix for p = 2). The pending KloostermanMomentsAndPotentialAutomorphy proposal plans Katz's monodromy computations, so the statement joins it; the new proof belongs to this paper's own route.

items.name: Dwork–Sperber: the Bessel F-isocrystal of rank n
items.statement: Let K = Q_p(μ_p), π ∈ K with π^{p−1} = −p matching ψ, λ = −π, n prime to p, and A^† the p-adic functions on P¹ overconvergent along ∞ (power series with radius of convergence > 1). There is a unique φ ∈ GL_n(A^†) with x (dφ/dx) φ^{−1} + φ M(x) φ^{−1} = p M(x^p) (so φ : F^*Be_n ≅ Be_n for F : x ↦ x^p), such that (ii) for a ∈ F_q^× with Teichmüller lift ã and φ_a = ∏_{i<deg a} φ(ã^{p^i}), ι Tr φ_a = Kl(n; a); and (iii) the eigenvalues α_i of φ_a satisfy |α_i|_p = p^{(n+1−2i) deg(a)/2} after reordering. (Be_n, φ) =: Be_n^† is an overconvergent F-isocrystal on G_{m,F_p}, the p-adic companion of Kl_n.
items.note: The GL_n base case of the paper's main theorem (Theorem 4.4.4 with 5.3.1).

items.name: Frenkel–Gross Bessel connection of a reductive group
items.statement: For split reductive Ǧ over K (char 0) with Borel B̌ and pinning, grade ǧ_aff = ǧ ⊗ A_K by Ad ρ(G_m) on ǧ and ȟ times the loop grading, ȟ the Coxeter number; ǧ_aff(1) = ⊕_{α̌ affine simple} ǧ_{aff,α̌}. For generic ξ̌ ∈ ǧ_aff(1) (every affine simple component nonzero), Be_Ǧ(ξ̌) = d + ξ̌ dx/x = d + (N + xE) dx/x on the trivial Ǧ-bundle on X = P¹ − {0, ∞}, with N principal nilpotent and E ∈ Σ_i ǧ_{−θ̌_i}; equivalently ∇ = d + N dx/x + λ^h E dx. It is a tensor functor Rep(Ǧ) → Conn(X), regular singular at 0 with principal unipotent monodromy and irregular at ∞ of maximal formal slope 1/ȟ. For δ̌ = (a, σ̌) ∈ G_m × Aut(Ǧ, B̌, Ť), Be_{Ǧ,V}(δ̌(ξ̌)) ≅ a^+Be_{Ǧ,σ̌V}(ξ̌), so Be_Ǧ(ξ̌) depends only on the Ť_ad-orbit of ξ̌, and these orbits are parametrised by ǧ_aff(1)//Ť_ad.
items.note: Frenkel–Gross, Ann. of Math. 170 (2009). No stage plans rigid irregular G-connections or the Frenkel–Gross connection.

items.name: Frenkel–Gross: differential Galois groups of Bessel connections
items.statement: For Ǧ almost simple the differential Galois group G_alg ⊂ Ǧ of Be_Ǧ over K̄ is connected, and up to central isogeny: A_{2n} ↦ A_{2n}; A_{2n−1}, C_n ↦ C_n; B_n, D_{n+1} (n ≥ 4) ↦ B_n; E_7 ↦ E_7; E_8 ↦ E_8; E_6, F_4 ↦ F_4; B_3, D_4, G_2 ↦ G_2. Be_Ǧ is rigid, and Aut(Be_Ǧ) = Z(Ǧ).
items.locator: §1.2.6, table (1.2.6.1), p. 6; §4.5.1, p. 51 (Frenkel–Gross, Cor. 9 and Cor. 10)
items.note: Recalled from Frenkel–Gross; used as the upper bound for G_geo in Theorem 4.5.2 and for the uniqueness of the Frobenius structure (Aut(Be_Ǧ) = Z(Ǧ), §4.4.1).

items.name: Frames, overconvergent (F-)isocrystals and rigid cohomology
items.statement: For a k-scheme X with a frame (Y, j, 𝒫, i) (X ⊂ Y open, Y ⊂ 𝒫 closed, 𝒫 a formal R-scheme smooth near X), j^† on sheaves on strict neighbourhoods of ]X[ in ]Y[; Isoc^†(X, Y/K) is the category of coherent j^†O-modules with a stratification (p_2^*M ≅ p_1^*M with the cocycle condition), independent of 𝒫, giving the convergent Isoc(X/K) for Y = X and Isoc^†(X/K) for Y a compactification; these embed fully faithfully into modules with overconvergent integrable connection. RΓ_rig(X/K, M) = RΓ(]X̄[, M ⊗ j^†Ω^•). With F_X^* induced by the s-th Frobenius and σ, an overconvergent F-isocrystal is (M, φ : F_X^*M ≅ M); Isoc^{††}(X/K) is the thick subcategory generated by objects admitting an s′-th Frobenius structure for some s | s′.
items.note: PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology RD.3 plans frames, tubes, strict neighbourhoods and overconvergent (F-)isocrystals with independence of the embedding; RD.4 plans rigid cohomology.

items.name: Dwork and Kummer F-isocrystals
items.statement: (i) For k = F_p, K = Q_p(μ_p), π^{p−1} = −p, the Dwork isocrystal A_π on A¹_k is j^†O_{P̂¹} with an overconvergent rank-one connection ±π dt, and its Frobenius structure for the lift t ↦ t^p is multiplication by θ_π(x) = exp(π(x − x^p))^{±1}; with the sign conventions made consistent (∇ = d − π dt with Frobenius θ_π), its Frobenius trace is ψ ∘ Tr, where ψ(1) ≡ 1 + π mod π², and A_ψ := A_π. (ii) For k = F_q, K = Q_q and a ∈ (1/(q−1))Z, the Kummer isocrystal K_a on G_m (∇ = d − a dx/x) has the Frobenius structure x^{−(q−1)a} for the lift x ↦ x^q, with trace χ^{−1} ∘ N, χ(x) = x̃^{(q−1)a}; replacing a by −a gives trace χ ∘ N, and K_χ denotes that object.
items.note: Berthelot, Astérisque 119–120 (1984) 1.4. The printed connections (d + π dt, d − a dx/x) and Frobenius maps (θ_π, t^{(q−1)a}) do not match (sourceIssues); the statement records the consistent version. RD.6's acceptance test uses an additive-character coefficient to check Fourier normalisation, so these examples are sources for RD.6.

items.name: Specialisation and cospecialisation between de Rham and rigid cohomology
items.statement: Let X be a smooth R-scheme of pure relative dimension d with a smooth proper compactification X̄ over R, (M, ∇) a coherent O_{X_K}-module with integrable connection whose analytification M^† = j^†(M^an) is overconvergent. There are a specialisation map ρ_M : RΓ_dR(X_K, M) → RΓ_rig(X_k/K, M^†) and a cospecialisation map ρ_{c,M} : RΓ_rig,c(X_k/K, M^†) → RΓ_dR,c(X_K, M) (with RΓ_dR,c defined by R lim over the powers of the boundary ideal), and ι_rig = ρ_M ∘ ι_dR ∘ ρ_{c,M} : RΓ_rig,c → RΓ_rig (Proposition 2.2.5).
items.note: Baldassarri–Berthelot §1 and André–Baldassarri App. D.2 for the maps; Proposition 2.2.5 is new, by rigid GAGA and the admissible covering of 𝒳̄ by 𝒳 and the tube of the boundary. RD.4 owns rigid cohomology with compact supports and its comparison maps, of which these are two.

items.name: Holonomic arithmetic D-modules and their six operations
items.statement: Over a base tuple 𝔗 = {k, R, K, L} (L/K algebraic) or an arithmetic tuple 𝔗_F = {k, R, K, L, s, σ}, D(X/L) (resp. D(X/L_F)) is Abe's triangulated category D^b_hol of holonomic complexes on a k-scheme X (for L = K and X quasi-projective, a full subcategory of the bounded coherent D^†_{𝒫,Q}-complexes built from Berthelot's D^†_{𝔛,Q}(†Z) and O_{𝔛,Q}(†Z) ≅ Sp_*(j^†O)), with the holonomic t-structure (Noetherian and Artinian heart Hol(X/L)), D(X/L) ≃ D^b(Hol(X/L)), and the six operations: ⊗ with unit L_X and internal ℋom (right adjoint), duality 𝔻_X with 𝔻𝔻 ≅ id, adjunctions (f^+, f_+), (f_!, f^!), f_! → f_+ an isomorphism for proper f, proper base change, the localisation triangles, f^! ≅ f^+(d)[2d] for smooth f of relative dimension d, Berthelot–Kashiwara, and the exact external product ⊠. Also: L-structures and scalar extension, invariance under finite extension of k, the σ-semilinear Frobenius pullback F_X^* with Hol(X/L_F) the objects with φ : F_X^*E ≅ E, and the constructible t-structure (heart Con(X), f^+ c-exact, f_+ left c-exact, stalks detect vanishing).
items.note: Recalled from Berthelot, Caro, Caro–Tsuzuki, Abe and Abe–Caro. Nothing in the atlas plans arithmetic D-modules or overholonomicity. (The printed text calls ℋom_X a left adjoint of ⊗.)

items.name: Smooth objects are overconvergent F-isocrystals; relative de Rham complexes
items.statement: For X smooth of dimension d, Sm(X/L) ⊂ Hol(X/L)[−d], and for L = K the specialisation S̃p_* = Sp_*(−d)[−d] gives Isoc^{††}(X/K) ≅ Sm(X/K) and F-Isoc^†(X/K) ≅ Sm(X/K_F), with f^+ matching pullback of isocrystals and f^!M ≅ f^+M(d)[2d] for smooth M on the target (d = dim X − dim Y). For a smooth morphism f : Spec B → Spec A of smooth affine R-schemes, f_+^dR(M) is computed by the relative de Rham complex DR_{B/A}(M, ∇); if f has a good compactification (a smooth f̄ between smooth projective R-schemes with ample boundary divisors) and M^† is overconvergent, then f_{k,+}(M^†) is computed by DR^†_{B/A}(M^†) = (M ⊗_{B_K} B^†) ⊗ Ω^•_{B/A}, and the relative specialisation DR_{B/A}(M, ∇) → DR^†_{B/A}(M^†) is D-linear.
items.note: Caro–Tsuzuki's overholonomicity of overconvergent F-isocrystals and Abe's 2.4.15; 𝒟^†-affinity (Huyghe 5.3.3). The relative specialisation is the input of Theorem 4.2.1.

items.name: Cohomology of holonomic modules: top degree and full faithfulness of smooth pullback
items.statement: (2.4.1) H^*(X, F) = ℋ^*f_+F and H^*_c(X, F) = ℋ^*f_!F are finite-dimensional; for X of dimension ≤ d and F constructible they live in degrees [0, 2d]; they agree with rigid cohomology (with compact supports) for smooth X with a smooth liftable compactification by a divisor; for smooth X, dim H⁰(X, L_X) is the number of connected components of X ⊗ k̄, with Frobenius permuting them; there is the excision sequence and the stratification spectral sequence. (Corollary 2.4.3, corrected) dim H^{2d}_c(X, L_X) is the number of d-dimensional irreducible components of X ⊗ k̄, on which Frobenius acts by q^d times the permutation of these components. (Proposition 2.4.4) If f : X → Y is smooth of relative dimension d, surjective with geometrically connected fibres, then f^+[d] : Hol(Y/L_▲) → Hol(X/L_▲) is fully faithful (▲ ∈ {∅, F}). (Lemma 2.4.5) For M ∈ D^{≤0} and N ∈ D^{≥0}, ℋom_X(M, N) ∈ cD^{≥0}.
items.note: Corollary 2.4.3 and 2.4.1(iii) are false as printed; Proposition 2.4.4 (the analogue of BBD 4.2.5) is proved through (2.4.6.2), whose reduction to a point by 'smooth base change' is not valid (sourceIssues).

items.name: Equivariant holonomic modules on schemes and ind-schemes
items.statement: For a smooth affine S-group scheme H with geometrically connected fibres acting on X → S, Hol_H(X) consists of (M, θ : act^+M ≅ pr_2^+M) with e^+θ = id and the cocycle condition; it is an abelian subcategory of Hol(X), Hol_H(X) → Hol(X) is fully faithful (Lemma 2.5.2), and q^+[d_H] : Hol(X̄) ≅ Hol_H(X) when X̄ = [X/H] is a separated k-scheme of finite type. (Lemma 2.5.3, corrected) If H_1 ⊂ H is closed normal, H/H_1 and H_1 are smooth, H_1 has geometrically connected fibres and H acts through H/H_1, then Hol_{H/H_1}(X) ≅ Hol_H(X). Twisted external products M ⊠̃ N on Y ×̃_S X for an H-torsor on Y; D and Hol on strict ind-schemes as 2-limits along closed pushforwards; Hol_H(𝒳) for pro-smooth H = lim H_j acting on an ind-scheme.
items.note: Lemma 2.5.3 is false without the connectedness of H_1 (sourceIssues); for L^+G the kernels of the jet groups are vector groups, so its uses are unaffected.

items.name: Intermediate extensions, weights and the decomposition theorem
items.statement: For a locally closed immersion u, u_{!+}E = Im(ℋ⁰u_!E → ℋ⁰u_+E); u_{!+} of an irreducible is the unique irreducible subobject of ℋ⁰u_+E, and every irreducible holonomic module is u_{!+} of a smooth one (Abe–Caro). (Corollary 2.6.2) For j : U → X open with complement i : Z → X, j_{!+}E is the unique extension F with i^+F ∈ D^{≤−1} and i^!F ∈ D^{≥1}; if X is smooth, U dense and F smooth, j_{!+}(F|_U) ≅ F. For k = F_q and ι : K̄ ≅ C, ι-mixed and ι-pure complexes are stable under the operations with the usual weight bounds (f_+, f^! raise, f_!, f^+ lower), u_{!+} preserves purity, and (Theorem 2.6.4) an ι-pure F-holonomic module is semisimple in Hol(X/L), and an ι-pure F-holonomic complex F is isomorphic in D(X/L) to ⊕_n ℋ^n(F)[−n].
items.note: The printed 2.6.2(ii) omits 'U dense' and the printed 2.6.4(ii) has [n] for [−n] (sourceIssues). The paper transfers Abe–Caro's decomposition from overholonomic modules to Hol(X/L) by 'the same argument'.

items.name: Nearby and vanishing cycles for arithmetic D-modules
items.statement: For f : X → A¹ with U = f^{−1}(G_m) and X_0 = f^{−1}(0), Abe–Caro's unipotent nearby cycles Ψ^un_f(F) = lim_n Ker(j_!(F ⊗ Log^n_f) → j_+(F ⊗ Log^n_f)) and vanishing cycles Φ^un_f are exact functors with a triangle i^+[−1] → Ψ^un_f → Φ^un_f, and (𝔻 ∘ Ψ^un_f)(1) ≅ Ψ^un_f ∘ 𝔻, 𝔻 ∘ Φ^un_f ≅ Φ^un_f ∘ 𝔻 (Proposition 2.7.2). Here Log^n has connection ∇(g log^{[i]}) = ∂g log^{[i]} + (g/t)log^{[i−1]} and Frobenius log^{[i]} ↦ q^i log^{[i]}. For a strictly henselian trait S in Pro(k), Abe's Ψ_f and Φ_f are the limits over henselian traits generically étale over S of the unipotent ones.
items.locator: §2.7, (2.7.1.1)–(2.7.4.2), Proposition 2.7.2, pp. 20–21 (Abe–Caro, Selecta Math. 24 (2018) §2; Abe, Nagoya Math. J. 236 (2019))
items.note: Recalled; no stage plans p-adic nearby cycles.

items.name: Universal local acyclicity for arithmetic D-modules
items.statement: For f : X → S with S smooth, M ∈ D(X) is locally acyclic (LA) over f if M ⊗ f^+N → (M ⊗̃ f^!N)(d_S)[2d_S] is an isomorphism for all N ∈ D(S), and ULA if this persists after every base change S′ → S of smooth k-schemes. (Proposition 2.8.3) Every M is ULA over Spec k; LA is preserved by smooth pullback (and descends along smooth surjections), by composition with smooth S → S′, by proper pushforward (and detected by closed immersions), and by duality. (Proposition 2.8.5) If D ⊂ S is a smooth divisor, i : Z = f^{−1}(D) → X, M LA over f with M|_U holonomic, then M ≅ j_{!+}(M|_U), i^+M[−1] ≅ i^!M(1)[1], both are holonomic, and i^+M[−1] is LA over f|_Z : Z → D. (Corollary 2.8.6) ULA objects have vanishing Φ^un and Φ after base change to any strictly henselian trait. (Corollary 2.8.7) On smooth X, an M that is ULA over the identity has smooth constructible (and holonomic) cohomology modules. The notions extend to ind-schemes and algebraic stacks, with nearby cycles for families over curves.
items.note: New in this paper, after Braverman–Gaitsgory. Proofs of 2.8.5(ii) and of the amplitude induction in 2.8.7 are left to the reader or compressed; the statements check out. (The proof of 2.8.3(i) writes the twist (2d_S) for (d_S), sourceIssues.)

items.name: Local monodromy of p-adic differential modules
items.statement: MC(R_K/K) is the category of differential modules over the Robba ring R_K, MC(R/K̄) its base change, and MCF those with Frobenius structure. Unipotent objects form MC^uni ≃ Vec^nil via (V, N) ↦ (V ⊗ R, ∇_N) with ∇_N(v ⊗ 1) = Nv ⊗ dx/x, so the Tannakian group of MC^uni is G_a; MCF is Tannakian with group 𝒢 ≅ I × G_a and slope filtration 𝒢^{>λ}, 𝒢^{>0} ≅ P (André). The p-adic local monodromy theorem holds, and the irregularity of an object of MCF equals the Swan conductor of the associated representation (Matsuda, Tsuzuki); the restriction functor |_x : Isoc^†(X/K) → MC(R_K/K) at a point at infinity of a curve.
items.locator: §2.9.1, (2.9.1.1), §2.9.3, (2.9.3.1), pp. 23–24 (André, Invent. Math. 148 (2002); Matsuda; Christol–Mebkhout; Kedlaya; Mebkhout; Tsuzuki)
items.note: RD.2 plans the p-adic local monodromy theorem and its logarithmic solutions; the Tannakian description of MC and MCF and the irregularity–Swan comparison are the extra precise leaves this paper uses.

items.name: Solutions, log extensions and nearby cycles at a unipotent point
items.statement: (2.9.2) With K{x} the functions on the open unit disc and d = x d/dx, a unipotent (M, ∇) ∈ MC(R_K/K) with associated (V, N) extends to a log ∇-module over K{x}, and Sol(M) = Hom_{K{x}}((M, ∇), (K{x}, d))^{∇=0} ≅ Coker(N)^∨ canonically. (2.9.3) If E ∈ Isoc^†(X/K) is unipotent at x, it extends to a log-isocrystal E^log with a log pole at x (Kedlaya, Compos. Math. 143 (2007) 6.3.2), whose fibre E^log_x is a (φ, N)-module with φ^{−1}Nφ = qN. (Proposition 2.9.4) For X = G_m ⊂ P¹ and E unipotent at 0, E^log_0 ≅ Ψ(E), with Frobenius, for the nearby cycle functor Ψ defined by the identity.
items.note: The printed (2.9.2.2) identifies Sol(M) with Coker(N) itself (sourceIssues); the uses in §§5 and A need only its dimension. Proposition 2.9.4 follows the arguments of Abe–Caro, Selecta 2.4(1) and Amer. J. Math. 3.4.19: for n at least the nilpotency index, v ↦ Σ_i (−N)^i v ⊗ log^{[i]} identifies V with the kernel defining Ψ, compatibly with Frobenius because Nφ = qφN.

items.name: Hyperbolic localisation for arithmetic D-modules
items.statement: Let X be quasi-projective with X ⊗ k̄ connected and normal, with a G_m-action; X^0 the fixed points, X^+ the attractor and X^− the repeller (Drinfeld–Gaitsgory), with sections f, f′ of π : X^+ → X^0, π′ : X^− → X^0 and g, g′ locally closed on components. For F ∈ D(X) put F^{!+} = f^!g^+F and F^{+!} = f′^+g′^!F; F is weakly equivariant if μ^+F ≅ L[−1] ⊠ F for a smooth L on G_m. (Theorem 2.10.2) (i) There is a canonical morphism ι_F : F^{+!} → F^{!+}, an isomorphism for weakly equivariant F. (ii) The canonical morphisms F^{!+} = f^!g^+F → π_!g^+F and π′_+g′^!F → f′^+g′^!F = F^{+!} are isomorphisms for weakly equivariant F.
items.note: Proved as in Braden via Sumihiro's equivariant embedding and Lemma 2.10.6 (Braden's Lemma 6) for a projective bundle, with details left to the reader. The printed (ii) has the first canonical map in the wrong direction, and the construction of ι_F in 2.10.3 asserts an isomorphism that fails for X = P¹ (sourceIssues).

items.name: Affine Grassmannian, Schubert varieties, convolution and Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannians
items.statement: For split reductive G over k = F_q: LG and L^+G are the fpqc sheaves R ↦ G(R((t))), G(R[[t]]); Gr_G = LG/L^+G is ind-projective (replaced by its reduction); for μ ∈ X_•(T)^+ the L^+G-orbit Gr_μ is smooth quasi-projective of dimension ⟨2ρ, μ⟩ with open immersion into its closure Gr_{≤μ} = ∪_{λ≤μ} Gr_λ, and L^+G acts on Gr_{≤μ} through a smooth connected jet group G_i. The convolution Grassmannian Gr ×̃ Gr = LG ×^{L^+G} Gr has the ind-proper map m([g, [h]]) = [gh]. For a smooth curve X, Gr_{G,X^n} (x ∈ X^n, a G-torsor on X_R and a trivialisation off Γ_x) is ind-projective over X^n, with Gr_X ≅ Gr × X for X = A¹, Gr_{X²} ×_{X²,Δ} X ≅ Gr_X, the S_2-equivariant factorisation Gr_{X²}|_U ≅ (Gr_X × Gr_X)|_U off the diagonal, and the global convolution m : Gr_X ×̃ Gr_X → Gr_{X²}, an isomorphism over U.
items.note: The geometry of classical (equal-characteristic) geometric Satake, as in Zhu's Park City notes §§1–3; GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.1 plans the Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannian over powers of a curve, convolution and collision/factorisation maps.

items.name: Semi-infinite orbits and Mirković–Vilonen dimensions
items.statement: Let S_λ = i(π^{−1}(L_λ)) and T_λ = i′(π′^{−1}(L_λ)) for Gr_T ← Gr_B → Gr_G and Gr_T ← Gr_{B^op} → Gr_G, L_λ = t^λ ∈ Gr_T(k). (i) S_{≤λ} = ∪_{λ′≤λ} S_{λ′} is closed and S_λ is open dense in it. (ii) For μ ∈ X_•(T)^+, Gr_μ ∩ S_λ (resp. Gr_μ ∩ T_λ) is non-empty iff L_λ ∈ Gr_{≤μ}, equivalently wλ ≤ μ for every w ∈ W (i.e. the dominant conjugate of λ is ≤ μ); it then has pure dimension ⟨ρ, λ + μ⟩ (resp. ⟨ρ, μ − λ⟩).
items.locator: §3.4.1–3.4.2, Proposition 3.4.2, p. 31 (Mirković–Vilonen 3.1–3.2; Zhu, Park City notes 5.3.6)
items.note: Stated with corrections: the printed proposition gives dimension ρ(λ + μ) for both intersections and the equivalent condition 'there exists w ∈ W with wλ ≤ μ' (sourceIssues). This is Mirković–Vilonen's geometry, part of the classical Satake proof GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.1 plans.

items.name: The Satake category of arithmetic D-modules
items.statement: Over the geometric base tuple {k, R, K, L}, Sat_G is the category of L^+G-equivariant holonomic arithmetic D-modules on Gr_G (a full subcategory of Hol(Gr_G)), with IC_μ = j_{μ,!+}(L_{Gr_μ}[⟨2ρ, μ⟩]) for μ ∈ X_•(T)^+; the convolution A_1 ⋆ A_2 = m_+(A_1 ⊠̃ A_2) uses the twisted external product on Gr ×̃ Gr.
items.note: Equivariant holonomic modules are those of §2.5.6; for A_X on Gr_X one uses A_X = A ⊠ L_X[1], which is ULA over X and gives a fully faithful ι : D(Gr) → D(Gr_X) (3.2.2, via Proposition 2.4.4).

items.name: Semisimplicity of the Satake category
items.statement: (Proposition 3.1.2) Sat_G is semisimple with simple objects IC_μ, μ ∈ X_•(T)^+. (Lemma 3.1.3) Sm(Gr_μ) is semisimple with simple object L_{Gr_μ}, and H¹(Gr_μ, L) = 0. (Lemma 3.1.4) The constructible cohomology cH^i(IC_μ) vanishes unless i ≡ dim Gr_μ mod 2.
items.note: Proof: Ext¹(IC_λ, IC_μ) = 0 in three cases (λ = μ by H¹ = 0 for the affine bundle Gr_μ → G/P_μ; comparable λ, μ by parity; incomparable by base change as in Baumann–Riche 4.3). Lemma 3.1.3 cites simple connectivity of Gr_μ ⊗ k̄ (Richarz), Abe's companions with finite determinant and Abe–Esnault's companion theorem with Čebotarev.

items.name: Fusion and the monoidal structure on Sat_G
items.statement: For A_1, A_2 ∈ Sat_X: (i) m_+(A_1 ⊠̃ A_2) ≅ j_{!+}(A_1 ⊠ A_2|_U) =: A_1 ⊠* A_2 on Gr_{X²}, ULA over X² and (L^+G)_{X²}-equivariant; (ii) Δ^+[−1](A_1 ⊠* A_2) ≅ Δ^!(A_1 ⊠* A_2)(1)[1], and the fusion product A_1 ⊛ A_2 := Δ^+[−1](A_1 ⊠* A_2) is ULA over X. For A_1, A_2 ∈ Sat_G: (A_1 ⋆ A_2)_X ≅ A_{1,X} ⊛ A_{2,X}; A_1 ⋆ A_2 is holonomic and lies in Sat_G; and (Sat_G, ⋆, IC_0) and (Sat_X, ⊛, IC_{0,X}) are monoidal categories.
items.note: Uses ULA descent along smooth surjections (Proposition 2.8.3; the printed proof cites (iii) where the smooth-descent part is meant) and Proposition 2.8.5(i). The Tate twist (1) of Proposition 2.8.5 is dropped in the printed (ii) (sourceIssues).

items.name: The hypercohomology fibre functor
items.statement: H^* : Sat_G → Vec_L, A ↦ ⊕_n H^n(Gr, A), is exact, faithful and monoidal: by Künneth q_+(A_X)[−1] ≅ π_+(A) ⊠ L_X, and q_+(A_1 ⊛ A_2)[−1] ≅ q_+(A_1)[−1] ⊗ q_+(A_2)[−1] (Lemma 3.3.2), compatibly with Frobenius structures (Remark 3.3.4). The swap of X² gives c′ : A_1 ⋆ A_2 ≅ A_2 ⋆ A_1 with H^*(c′) the super-commutativity constraint s ⊗ t ↦ (−1)^{ij} t ⊗ s.
items.note: Faithfulness also uses H^*(IC_μ) ≠ 0, which follows from Proposition 3.4.3. The last step of Lemma 3.3.2 (an isomorphism on U and on Δ^!) needs, besides the distinguished triangle, that the cohomology modules are constant on A² — true since each is j_{!+} of its restriction to U.

items.name: Weight functors via hyperbolic localisation
items.statement: (Proposition 3.4.3) (i) For A ∈ Sat_G, H^i_c(S_λ, A) ≅ H^i_{T_λ}(Gr_G, A), and both vanish for i ≠ ⟨2ρ, λ⟩. (ii) dim H^{⟨2ρ,λ⟩}_c(S_λ, IC_μ) is the number of irreducible components of S_λ ∩ Gr_μ over k̄; over the arithmetic tuple {k, R, K, L, s, id_L}, Frobenius acts on it by q^{⟨ρ,λ+μ⟩} when these components are defined over k. (iii) H^i(Gr_G, A) ≅ ⊕_λ H^i_c(S_λ, A). (Proposition 3.4.4) H^{⟨2ρ,λ⟩}_c(S_λ, A_1 ⋆ A_2) ≅ ⊕_{λ_1+λ_2=λ} H^{⟨2ρ,λ_1⟩}_c(S_{λ_1}, A_1) ⊗ H^{⟨2ρ,λ_2⟩}_c(S_{λ_2}, A_2), proved by extending S_λ, T_λ to Gr_{X²} (3.4.5–3.4.6).
items.note: Braden's theorem for arithmetic D-modules (Theorem 2.10.2) replaces the ℓ-adic one in Mirković–Vilonen 3.5–3.6. The Frobenius claim in (ii) rests on Corollary 2.4.3, which needs the top-dimensional components of S_λ ∩ Gr_μ to be defined over k; 3.4.6 has a uniform index shift; the normality claims of 3.4.5 fail when p divides |π_1(G_der)| (all in sourceIssues).

items.name: Symmetric monoidal structure and neutral Tannakian category
items.statement: With the parity p(μ) = ⟨2ρ, μ⟩ mod 2, H^i(Gr, IC_μ) = 0 for i ≢ p(μ) mod 2, and c_{A_1,A_2} = (−1)^{p(A_1)p(A_2)}c′_{A_1,A_2} (extended by semisimplicity) makes (Sat_G, ⋆, IC_0, c) symmetric monoidal with H^* a tensor functor (Proposition 3.4.8); with H^* it is a neutral Tannakian category over L (Theorem 3.5.1), whose group G̃ = Aut^⊗H^* is a connected reductive group over L (Proposition 3.5.2: IC_{μ_1+μ_2} is a summand of IC_{μ_1} ⋆ IC_{μ_2}, so Sat_G is finitely generated; no non-trivial tensor subcategory has finitely many simple objects; semisimplicity).
items.note: Following Mirković–Vilonen after Remark 6.2 and Zhu's notes 5.2.9. The printed parity map is written μ ↦ (−1)^{2ρ(μ)} ∈ Z/2Z (sourceIssues).

items.name: Geometric Satake for arithmetic D-modules: the dual group
items.statement: The Tannakian group G̃ of (Sat_G, H^*) is the Langlands dual group of G over L: for a maximal torus T̃ its root datum is dual to that of (G, T). Steps: the torus case (Gr_{T,red} is discrete, indexed by X_•(T)); the constant-term functor CT : Sat_G → Sat_T, A ↦ (H^*_c(S_λ, A))_λ, with H^*_G ≅ H^*_T ∘ CT a tensor functor, giving a closed subtorus Ť ≅ T̃ ⊂ G̃ (Deligne–Milne 2.21(b)) that is maximal (Lemma 3.5.6); the Borel with 2ρ dominant has X^•(Ť)^+ = X_•(T)^+ and simple roots the simple coroots of G, which determine the root datum. Hence Hol_{L^+G}(Gr_G/K) ≅ Rep(Ǧ) as monoidal categories.
items.note: Theorem 1.3.6(i) of the introduction. The p-adic realisation of the motivic Satake equivalence is not available, so the proof is carried out directly with arithmetic D-modules.

items.name: Tannakian categories with a semilinear Z-action
items.statement: Let (C, ω) be a neutralised Tannakian category over L with σ^n-semilinear tensor autoequivalences τ_n, isomorphisms α_n : ω ∘ τ_n ≅ σ^n ∘ ω and compatible ε : τ_m ∘ τ_n ≅ τ_{m+n}; this defines ι : Z → Aut(H(L)), H the Tannakian group. C^Z is the category of (X, {c_n : τ_nX ≅ X}) with c_{n+m} = c_n ∘ τ_n(c_m). (Proposition 3.6.4) For split reductive H over L, Rep_L(H) → Rep_L(H(L)) is fully faithful. (Proposition 3.6.5) (i) C^Z is a Tannakian category over L_0 = L^{σ=1} neutralised by ω over L; (ii) if H is split reductive, ω induces C^Z ≅ Rep°_{L,σ}(H(L) ⋊ Z), the σ-semilinear representations whose restriction to H(L) is algebraic.
items.note: After Richarz–Zhu's appendix to Zhu's ramified Satake paper. Essential surjectivity in 3.6.5(ii) is left to the reader; with ι as defined, the representation (3.6.5.3) is one of the semidirect product formed through ι^{−1} in the standard convention, a relabelling.

items.name: Geometric Satake with Frobenius structures
items.statement: Let F-Sat_G be the category of objects of Sat_G with a Frobenius structure for an arithmetic tuple {k, R, K, L, t, σ}. (i) F-Sat_G ≅ Sat_G^Z is a Tannakian category over L_0 neutralised by H^* over L, and neutral if t = s and σ = id_L. (ii) F-Sat_G ≅ Rep°_{L,σ}(Ǧ(L) ⋊ Z), compatibly with fibre functors. For t = s, σ = id_L and p^{1/2} ∈ L, the Weil-normalised objects IC^Weil_μ = j_{μ,!+}(L_{Gr_μ}[⟨2ρ, μ⟩])(⟨ρ, μ⟩) (μ dominant) have weight 0, their direct sums form a subcategory S closed under ⋆, and Sat : Rep_L(Ǧ) ≅ Sat_G ≅ S. The action of Aut(G) on Gr_G gives ι : Aut(G) → Aut(Ǧ) factoring through Out(G) ≅ Aut^†(Ǧ, B̌, Ť, N) for a natural pinning, with σ^*Sat(V) ≅ Sat(ι(σ)V).
items.note: Theorem 1.3.6(ii). Closure of S under ⋆ uses that Frobenius acts on H^i(IC^Weil_μ) by q^{i/2} (Proposition 3.4.3(ii)) and that an object whose summands are IC_ν ⊗ (M_ν, φ_ν) is determined by the Frobenius on its cohomology. Lemma 3.6.10 follows HNY B.2 and Richarz–Zhu A.6. The printed IC^Weil_μ applies j_{!+} before the shift (sourceIssues).

items.name: Heinloth–Ngô–Yun level groups and moduli of bundles on P¹
items.statement: For split reductive G with B ⊃ T and coordinate x on P¹ (y = x^{−1} at ∞): I(0) = {g ∈ G(k[[y]]) : g(0) ∈ B}, I(1) its pro-unipotent radical, I(2) = Z(G)(1)[I(1), I(1)] (so I(2) = [I(1), I(1)] for G semisimple and I(2) = I(1) for a torus), I(i)^op ⊂ G(k[[x]]) the opposite ones; I(1)/I(2) ≅ ⊕_{α affine simple} U_α, and Ω = N_{G(k((x)))}(I(0)^op)/I(0)^op. G(m, n) is the group scheme on P¹ equal to G × X on X with G(m, n)(O_0) = I(m)^op and G(m, n)(O_∞) = I(n). The connected components of Bun_{G(0,n)} are in bijection with Ω via Hecke modifications Hk_γ at 0, with base points i_γ = Hk_γ(⋆), and j : Ω × I(1)/I(2) → Bun_{G(0,2)} is the open immersion of the big cell.
items.note: The paper's I(2) differs from HNY 1.2 when G is not semisimple but agrees for GL_n. GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.0 plans Bun_G with level structures for a smooth model on a curve; this item is the specific Iwahori/Moy–Prasad data at 0 and ∞, imported from GS.0's general construction.

items.name: Geometric Hecke operators and Hecke eigen-modules for holonomic D-modules
items.statement: Hk^X_{G(m,n)} is the stack of (E_1, E_2, x, β) with E_i ∈ Bun_{G(m,n)}, x ∈ X and β : E_1 ≅ E_2 off Γ_x, with pr_1, pr_2 : Hk → Bun, Bun × X and a smooth atlas U → Bun trivialising both projections as U × Gr_{G,X}. For V ∈ Rep(Ǧ), IC_V on Hk is the smooth descent of K_{U×X} ⊠ Sat(V), and Hk_V(M) = pr_{2,!}(pr_{1,V}^+(M) ⊗ IC_V) : D(Bun_{G(m,n)}) → D(Bun_{G(m,n)} × X). A Ǧ-valued overconvergent (F-)isocrystal on X is a tensor functor E : Rep(Ǧ) → Sm(X/L) (resp. Sm(X/L_F)); a Hecke eigen-module with eigenvalue E is a holonomic M with isomorphisms Hk_V(M) ≅ M ⊠ E_V compatible with the tensor structure and composition of Hecke operators (Beilinson–Drinfeld 5.4.2).
items.note: Uses the geometric Satake equivalence for arithmetic D-modules of §3 (Sat) and the six operations on stacks of §2.

items.name: Cleanness of the Artin–Schreier module on the big cell
items.statement: Fix ψ and π with π^{p−1} = −p, the Dwork F-isocrystal A_ψ on A¹ and a generic linear function φ : I(1)/I(2) → A¹ (an isomorphism on each U_α); A_{ψφ} = φ^+A_ψ. (i) j_{γ,!}(A_{ψφ}) → j_{γ,+}(A_{ψφ}) is an isomorphism. (ii) M ↦ j_{γ,!}(A_{ψφ}) ⊠ M is an equivalence Hol(X) ≅ Hol(Bun^γ_{G(0,2)} × X)^{I(1)/I(2), A_{ψφ}}, with quasi-inverse N ↦ (i_γ × id)^+N ≅ (i_γ × id)^!N. A_{ψφ} denotes (j_{γ,!}(A_{ψφ})[dim Bun])_{γ∈Ω}.
items.note: The arithmetic D-module version of Heinloth–Ngô–Yun Lemma 2.3, by the same argument.

items.name: Kloosterman F-isocrystals as Hecke eigenvalues
items.statement: (Theorem 4.1.5) For (m, n) = (0, 2), A_{ψφ} is a Hecke eigen-module whose eigenvalue is a Ǧ-valued overconvergent F-isocrystal Kl^rig_Ǧ(ψφ) : Rep(Ǧ) → Sm(X/L_F), and each Kl^rig_{Ǧ,V}(ψφ) is pure of weight 0. (Lemma 4.1.6) Hk_V(A_{ψφ})[1] is holonomic. Concretely, with GR ≅ Gr_G × X, GR°_V its part over the big cell and p_1°, p_2° as in (4.1.8.2), E_V ≅ p°_{2,!}(p°^+_{1,V}(A_{ψφ}) ⊗ IC_V|_{GR°}) and the map to p°_{2,+} of the same object is an isomorphism.
items.note: Proof: cleanness on the Hecke stack, ULA of IC_V over X (so its vanishing cycles vanish), commutation of vanishing cycles with smooth pullback and proper pushforward (Abe), and smoothness of an object with vanishing Φ; purity from the equality of ! and + pushforwards.

items.name: Trivial functoriality, exceptional isomorphisms and symmetries of Kl^rig
items.statement: (i) If G′ → G induces G′_ad ≅ G_ad, then Kl^rig_{Ǧ′} ≅ Kl^rig_Ǧ ∘ Res along Ǧ → Ǧ′; hence Kl^rig_{SL_2,Sym²} ≅ Kl^rig_{SO_3,Std}, Kl^rig_{Sp_4, ker(∧²→1)} ≅ Kl^rig_{SO_5,Std}, Kl^rig_{SO_4,Std} ≅ Kl^rig_{SL_2×SL_2, Std⊠Std} and Kl^rig_{SO_6,Std} ≅ Kl^rig_{SL_4,∧²}. (ii) For δ = (a, σ) ∈ (G_m × Aut(G, B, T))(k), Kl^rig_{Ǧ,V}(ψ(φ∘δ)) ≅ a^+Kl^rig_{Ǧ,ι(σ^{−1})V}(ψφ); so Kl^rig_Ǧ(ψφ) depends only on the T_ad-orbit of φ, and Kl_Ǧ(ψ_aφ) ≅ (a^h)^+Kl_Ǧ(ψφ). (iii) If Ǧ is almost simple not of type A_{2n}, or p = 2, then Kl^rig_{Ǧ,V} ≅ Kl^rig_{Ǧ,ι(σ^{−1})V} for σ ∈ Out(G); if G is of type A_{2n} and p > 2, Kl^rig_{Ǧ,V} ≅ (−1)^+Kl^rig_{Ǧ,V^∨}.
items.note: Proved from the G_m × Aut(G, B, T)-action on the Hecke diagram and on the Satake category (Lemma 3.6.10: ι : Aut(G) → Aut(Ǧ, B̌, Ť, N)).

items.name: Kloosterman F-isocrystals with a multiplicative character, and the ℓ-adic and de Rham variants
items.statement: (4.1.11) For T̃ = N_{G(k((x)))}(I(0)^op)/I(1)^op (an extension of Ω by T), a splitting s : T ⋊ Ω ≅ T̃ and a character χ : T(k) → K^×, the same construction on Bun_{G(1,2)} with K_χ ⊠ A_{ψφ} gives Kl^rig_Ǧ(ψφ, χ, s), pure of weight 0, with Kl^rig_Ǧ(ψφ) = Kl^rig_Ǧ(ψφ, 1, s). (4.1.12) Heinloth–Ngô–Yun's ℓ-adic Ǧ-local system Kl^{et,ℓ}_Ǧ(ψφ, χ, s) has the same Frobenius traces as Kl^rig_Ǧ(ψφ, χ, s) at every closed point, via ι : K̄ ≅ Q̄_ℓ (trace formula and Gabber–Fujiwara ℓ-independence). (4.1.13) Replacing AS_ψ by E_λ = K⟨x, ∂_x⟩/(∂_x − λ) and K_χ by the Kummer D-module gives a Ǧ-connection Kl^dR_Ǧ(λφ, χ, s) : Rep(Ǧ) → Conn(X_K) (HNY 2.6).
items.note: The ℓ-adic Kloosterman sheaves of Heinloth–Ngô–Yun (Ann. of Math. 177 (2013)) are not planned anywhere; the trace comparison uses Abe–Caro's trace formula and ℓ-independence.

items.name: Kl^dR and Kl^rig agree after analytification
items.statement: Over R with residue field k and L = K, for a generic linear function φ over R (generic modulo the maximal ideal), a character χ̄ : T(k) → K^× lifting to χ : T → G_m, and a splitting s over R, for every V ∈ Rep(Ǧ) there is a canonical isomorphism of O_X-modules with connection ι_V : (Kl^dR_{Ǧ,V}(−πφ, χ, s))^† ≅ Kl^rig_{Ǧ,V}(φ, χ̄, s), compatible with tensor structures; here O_X = O_{P̂¹,Q}(†{0, ∞}).
items.note: Minuscule V: the specialisation map H*_dR((GR°_{V,s})_K, M_s) → H*_rig((GR°_{V,s})_k, 𝓜_s) is an isomorphism concentrated in degree 0 (Lemma 4.2.3), then the relative specialisation map and faithful flatness of A^† → A^0. Quasi-minuscule V: the same for intermediate extensions from the smooth locus (Lemma 4.2.6), with overconvergence checked on a dense open (Ogus 2.16, Kedlaya 6.3.2). General V: direct summands of tensor products of minuscule and quasi-minuscule representations.

items.name: Fibrewise comparison of twisted de Rham and rigid cohomology
items.statement: (Lemma 4.2.3) For V minuscule, s ∈ X(k) lifted to X(R), M = p_1^+(E_{−π})[dim Gr_λ] and 𝓜 = p_1^+(A_ψ)[dim Gr_λ], the specialisation map H*_dR((GR°_{V,s})_K, M_s) → H*_rig((GR°_{V,s})_k, 𝓜_s) is an isomorphism and both vanish outside degree 0. (Lemma 4.2.6) For V quasi-minuscule, with τ = p_2° ∘ j : GR°°_V → X on the smooth locus: (i) τ_{k,+}(𝓜)[1] and τ_{K,+}(M)[1] are holonomic; (ii) the specialisation map induces H⁰_dR((GR°_{V,s})_K, j_{!+}(M_s)) ≅ H⁰((GR°_{V,s})_k, j_{!+}(𝓜_s)).
items.note: Uses the compatibility of specialisation and cospecialisation maps (Proposition 2.2.5), cleanness (4.1.8.4) and the smooth compactification Gr_λ (resp. the Demazure-type resolution of Gr_{≤λ}, Ngô–Polo §7).

items.name: Zhu: Kloosterman connections are Frenkel–Gross connections
items.statement: There is a canonical isomorphism of affine schemes g*_aff(1)//T ≅ ǧ_aff(1)//Ť such that if the T_ad-orbit of λφ matches the Ť_ad-orbit of ξ̌ then Kl^dR_Ǧ(λφ) ≅ Be_Ǧ(ξ̌) as Ǧ-bundles with connection on X. The isomorphism is the one compatible with the Hitchin maps to Γ(X, c* ×^{G_m} ω_X) ≅ Γ(X, č ×^{G_m} ω_X); for G almost simple, λφ matches ξ̌ iff λ^h P_r(φ) = P̌_r(ξ̌) for matching invariant polynomials of degree h = ȟ.
items.note: Proof: quantise the classical duality to U(Lie I(1)/I(2))^T ≅ Fun Op_ǧ (Zhu 2017, Lemma 21), where Op_ǧ is the space of Ǧ_ad-opers on X regular singular with principal unipotent monodromy at 0 and of slope ≤ 1/ȟ at ∞ (Beilinson–Drinfeld §3), and apply the Galois-to-automorphic direction of Beilinson–Drinfeld (Zhu 2017) for Ǧ adjoint. For general Ǧ: a de Rham Ǧ-local system inducing Be_{Ǧ_ad} with unipotent monodromy at 0 is unique, since two differ by a Ž-local system on A¹, which must be trivial. Strengthens Zhu, Selecta Math. 23 (2017), which had the adjoint case.

items.name: The Bessel F-isocrystal of a reductive group
items.statement: With λ = −π and ξ̌ matching −πφ, fix x and a pinning N; there is a unique E = E_φ ∈ Σ_i ǧ_{−θ̌_i} with Kl^dR_Ǧ(1·φ) ≅ d + (N + xE)dx/x, and then Kl^dR_Ǧ(−πφ) ≅ d + (N + (−π)^h xE)dx/x = Be_Ǧ(ξ̌). By Theorem 4.2.1 this endows Be^†_Ǧ(ξ̌) (Be_Ǧ(ξ̌) composed with (−)^†) with a Frobenius structure φ : F^*_{X_k} ∘ Be^†_Ǧ ≅ Be^†_Ǧ, independent of the chosen isomorphism because Aut(Be_Ǧ) = Z(Ǧ); (Be^†_Ǧ(ξ̌), φ) : Rep(Ǧ) → F-Iso^†(X_k/K) is the Bessel F-isocrystal of Ǧ. Its restriction at 0 has p-adic exponents 0, is equivalent to d + dρ(N) over the Robba ring and is unipotent, so Be^†_Ǧ factors through log convergent F-isocrystals on (A¹_k, 0) with nilpotent residue, overconvergent along ∞.
items.note: The object in the title. The log extension uses Kedlaya's p-adic differential equations 12.6.1, 13.7.1 and Kedlaya, Compos. Math. 143 (2007), 6.3.2.

items.name: Frobenius structure on Bessel connections with Kloosterman traces
items.statement: Let A^† = Γ(P¹_k, O_{P̂¹,Q}(†{∞})). There is a unique φ ∈ Ǧ(A^†) with x (dφ/dx) φ^{−1} + Ad_φ(N + (−π)^h xE) = q(N + (−π)^h x^q E) such that, via a fixed K̄ ≅ Q̄_ℓ, Tr(φ_a, V) = Tr(Frob_a, Kl^{et,ℓ}_{Ǧ,V,ā}(ψφ)) for every a ∈ |X| and V ∈ Rep(Ǧ), where φ_a = ∏_{i<deg a} φ(ã^{q^i}). In particular the analytification of Be_Ǧ is overconvergent and Be^†_Ǧ : Rep(Ǧ) → F-Iso^†(G_{m,F_p}/K) is a p-adic companion of Kl_Ǧ.
items.note: The first main theorem of the paper, assembled from Theorems 4.1.5, 4.2.1 and 4.3.3 and the trace comparison of §4.1.12.

items.name: Frobenius of the Bessel F-isocrystal at 0
items.statement: Let 2ρ be the sum of the positive coroots in X_•(Ť). Then φ_0 = 2ρ(√q) in the set of semisimple conjugacy classes of Ǧ(K̄).
items.note: φ_0^{−1}Nφ_0 = qN gives φ_0 = ερ(q) with ε central; ε = 1 by comparing the Frobenius eigenvalues on the nearby cycles Ψ(Be^†_{Ǧ,V}) with those of Ψ(Kl^{et,ℓ}_{Ǧ,V}) (ℓ-independence), whose weight graded pieces have dimension dim H^{2i}(Gr_G, IC_V) and Frobenius q^i (Görtz–Haines, HNY 4.3).

items.name: Geometric, arithmetic and differential monodromy groups of Be_Ǧ
items.statement: With L = K̄, ⟨Be^†_Ǧ⟩ ⊂ Sm(X_k/K̄), ⟨Be^†_Ǧ, φ⟩ ⊂ Sm(X_k/K̄_F) and ⟨Be_Ǧ⟩ ⊂ Conn(X_K̄) are the full subcategories of subquotients of the Be^†_{Ǧ,V}, (Be^†_{Ǧ,V}, φ) and Be_{Ǧ,V}. They are Tannakian over K̄, with groups G_geo, G_arith and G_alg, and the tensor functors from Rep(Ǧ) give closed immersions G_geo → G_arith → Ǧ and G_geo → G_alg → Ǧ.
items.note: Tannakian formalism for overconvergent (F-)isocrystals (Crew; Deligne, Catégories tannakiennes).

items.name: Monodromy groups of Bessel F-isocrystals
items.statement: Let G be split almost simple over R, Ǧ its dual over K̄, Σ the outer automorphism group of Ǧ (a subgroup of Out(ǧ) depending on the isogeny type). (i) If Ǧ is not of type A_{2n} or char k > 2, G_geo → G_alg is an isomorphism; in particular G_geo ≅ Ǧ^{Σ,∘} if Ǧ is not of type A_{2n} (n ≥ 1), nor B_3, nor D_{2n} (n ≥ 2) with Σ ≠ Out(ǧ); G_geo = Ǧ if Ǧ is of type A_{2n}; G_geo ≅ G_2 if Ǧ is of type B_3 or D_4; G_geo ≅ Spin_{4n−1} if Ǧ is of type D_{2n} with Σ trivial (n ≥ 3). (ii) If Ǧ = SL_{2n+1} and char k = 2, G_geo(Be^†_{SL_{2n+1}}) = G_geo(Be^†_{SO_{2n+1}}), which is SO_{2n+1} for n ≠ 3 and G_2 for n = 3, so G_geo ≠ G_alg. (iii) G_geo → G_arith is always an isomorphism.
items.note: The first bullet of (i) as printed excludes A_{2n} only for n ≥ 2, so for A_2 it contradicts the second bullet; the statement above uses the reading the proof supports (sourceIssues). Proof: G_geo contains the image of G_a with Lie algebra N (principal unipotent at 0), so G°_geo is semisimple containing a principal PGL_2; Lemma 4.5.5 excludes PGL_2; comparison with G_alg (Frenkel–Gross); symmetries §4.1.10 and φ_0 (Proposition 4.4.5) for G_arith; for A_{2n}, p > 2, a descent to G_m/μ_2 contradicting Swan conductor 1; for A_{2n}, p = 2, the appendix.

items.name: Wild ramification at ∞ and exclusion of a principal PGL_2
items.statement: (Lemma 4.5.3) Restriction to ∞ gives I_∞ × G_a → G_geo, non-trivial on the wild inertia P_∞. (4.5.4) G°_geo is semisimple (Be^†_{Ǧ,V} is pure of weight 0, hence geometrically semisimple) and almost simple, with Lie algebra in one of the chains sl_2 → sp_{2n} → sl_{2n}; sl_2 → so_{2n+1} → sl_{2n+1}, so_{2n+2}; sl_2 → g_2 → so_7 → sl_7, so_8; sl_2 → f_4 → e_6; sl_2 → e_7; sl_2 → e_8. (Lemma 4.5.5) If Ǧ is not of type A_1, and not of type A_2 when p = 2, the image of G_geo in Ǧ_ad is not contained in a principal PGL_2: Irr_∞(Be^†_{Ǧ,Ad}) ≤ (ȟ + 1)r/ȟ < r + 1 by Baldassarri's bound, while Ad ≅ ⊕_i S^{2ℓ_i} over the principal PGL_2 with {ℓ_1, …, ℓ_r} the exponents of ǧ would force Irr_∞ ≥ r + 1.
items.note: The printed proof says {ℓ_i + 1} are the exponents; the decomposition requires {ℓ_i} (sourceIssues). Cases: P_∞ acting through G_m ⊂ PGL_2 (Irr(S^{2ℓ}) ≥ ℓ − ⌊ℓ/p⌋) or, for p = 2, I_∞ ↠ A_4 (decompositions of S^{2ℓ}, ℓ ≤ 7, into A_4-representations). Baldassarri's comparison of p-adic and formal slopes (André, Filtrations de type Hasse–Arf 3.2).

items.name: Monodromy of ℓ-adic Kloosterman sheaves via companions
items.statement: For Ǧ almost simple, the geometric and arithmetic monodromy groups of Kl^{et,ℓ}_Ǧ(ψφ) over Q̄_ℓ are those of Theorem 4.5.2. This reproves Heinloth–Ngô–Yun Theorem 3 without their restrictions on small p, and Katz's theorem for Kl_n.
items.note: The semisimplifications of Kl^{et,ℓ}_{Ǧ,V} and Be^†_{Ǧ,V} have the same Frobenius traces, so D'Addezio (arXiv:1711.06669, 4.1.1, 4.3.2) gives G^ℓ_arith ↠ G_arith, and both are closed subgroups of Ǧ.

items.name: Local monodromy of Bessel F-isocrystals at ∞
items.statement: For Ǧ almost simple of rank r: (i) H^i(P¹, j_{!+}(Be^†_{Ǧ,Ad})) = 0 for all i; (ii) Irr_∞(Be^†_{Ǧ,Ad}) = r, Ad^{I_∞} = 0 and the nilpotent monodromy N_∞ = 0, so I_∞ → Ǧ is a simple wild parameter in the sense of Gross–Reeder. The same holds for Kl_Ǧ, with no restriction on p (recovering HNY Prop. 5.3). When p ∤ #W the only non-zero break of Be^†_{Ǧ,Ad} at ∞ is 1/ȟ (Gross–Reeder 5.6); for p = 2 and n odd the local parameter of Be^†_{SO_n} at ∞ is the Gross–Reeder parameter of §6.3, with I_∞ acting on the SO_3 case through A_4, which recovers André's result on Be^†_2 at p = 2.
items.note: Proof: H⁰ = H² = 0 (G_geo has no invariants on Ad, D^†-affinity, Poincaré duality), dim H¹_c = Irr_∞ ≤ r by Grothendieck–Ogg–Shafarevich and (4.5.5.1), and the localisation sequence with dim Ad^N = r at 0 forces Ad^{I_∞, N_∞} = 0.

items.name: Uniqueness of the Frobenius structure
items.statement: Any two Frobenius structures on Be^†_Ǧ(ξ̌) (isomorphisms of tensor functors F^*_X ∘ Be^†_Ǧ ≅ Be^†_Ǧ) differ by an element of the centre Z_Ǧ(K̄).
items.note: Tannakian formalism: the difference is an element of Ǧ(K̄) centralising G_geo, and Z_Ǧ(G_geo) = Z_Ǧ.

items.name: Functoriality of Bessel F-isocrystals
items.statement: Let Ǧ′ ⊂ Ǧ be dual groups of split almost simple G′, G over R appearing in the same line of table (1.2.6.1), the inclusion preserving pinnings (so ǧ′_aff(1) ⊂ ǧ_aff(1)); let φ′ be a generic linear function of G′ over R and ξ̌ ∈ ǧ′_aff(1) match −πφ′. (i) There is a generic linear function φ of G over R such that −πφ matches ξ̌ ∈ ǧ_aff(1). (ii) With (Be^†_{Ǧ′}(ξ̌), φ′) and (Be^†_Ǧ(ξ̌), φ) constructed from φ′ and φ, (Be^†_Ǧ(ξ̌), φ) is the push-out of (Be^†_{Ǧ′}(ξ̌), φ′) along Ǧ′ → Ǧ.
items.note: (i): the matching φ over K is integral, since writing Be_{Ǧ,Ad}(ξ̌) = d + (N + cxE)dx/x against an integral reference, a non-unit c would give an irreducible summand a solution at 0 of convergence radius ≠ 1 and hence a trivial quotient. (ii): the Frobenius structures differ by a central ε (Lemma 5.1.1), and ε = 1 by Proposition 4.4.5. The printed (ii) writes φ for the Frobenius structure of Be^†_{Ǧ′} (sourceIssues).

items.name: Heinloth–Ngô–Yun functoriality conjecture
items.statement: Fix ψ and Ǧ′ ⊂ Ǧ (over Q̄_ℓ) in the same line of table (1.2.6.1). For every generic linear function φ′ of G′ over k there is a generic linear function φ of G over k such that Kl^{et,ℓ}_Ǧ(ψφ) is isomorphic to the push-out of Kl^{et,ℓ}_{Ǧ′}(ψφ′) along Ǧ′ ⊂ Ǧ as ℓ-adic Ǧ-local systems on X_k. This is HNY Conjecture 7.3.
items.note: Proof: reduce to Ǧ simply connected; lift φ′ to R and take φ as in Proposition 5.1.3 (the printed proof swaps φ and φ′, sourceIssues); equal traces for V ∈ Rep(Ǧ) extend to all representations of G_geo because K(Rep Ǧ) ⊗ Q̄_ℓ → K(Rep Ǧ^Σ) ⊗ Q̄_ℓ is surjective, so the two representations π_1 → G_geo are conjugate in GL(W) by an element inducing an automorphism of G_geo that fixes G_geo//G_geo, hence inner.

items.name: Hypergeometric sums, hypergeometric D-modules and multiplicative convolution
items.statement: For ψ, n ≥ 1 and multiplicative characters ρ = (ρ_1, …, ρ_m) of k^×, H_ψ(n, ρ)(a) = Σ ψ(Tr(Σ_i x_i − Σ_j y_j)) ∏_j ρ_j^{−1}(N(y_j)) over (x, y) ∈ (k′^×)^{n+m} with ∏ x_i = a ∏ y_j (Katz 8.2.7 with n trivial characters). For M, N ∈ D(G_{m,k}/L) and μ the multiplication, M ⋆ N = μ_!(M ⊠ N). For n > m ≥ 0, π as above and β ∈ ((1/(q−1))Z − Z)^m, Hyp_π(n, β) = δ^n − (−1)^{n+mp}π^{n−m} x ∏_j (δ − β_j) with δ = x d/dx, and DHyp_π(n, β) = D^†_{P̂¹,Q}({0, ∞})/D^† Hyp_π(n, β), which depends only on ψ and ρ (written DHyp_ψ(n, ρ)).
items.note: Katz, Exponential sums and differential equations (1990) §§5.3, 8.2; Miyatani, Amer. J. Math. 142 (2020). No stage plans hypergeometric sums, sheaves or F-isocrystals.

items.name: Miyatani: hypergeometric F-isocrystals
items.statement: Fix Q̄_p ≅ C. (i) DHyp_π(n, β) underlies a pure overconvergent F-isocrystal on G_{m,k} of rank n and weight n + m − 1. (ii) Its Frobenius structure is unique up to a scalar. (iii) Its Frobenius trace on G_{m,k} is (−1)^{n+m−1}H_ψ(n, ρ), with ρ_i(ξ) = ξ̃^{(q−1)β_i} for the Teichmüller lift ξ̃.
items.locator: §5.2, Theorem 5.2.2, p. 57 (Miyatani, Main Theorem; (ii) by the method of 4.2.1)
items.note: Miyatani constructs the Frobenius by multiplicative convolution of arithmetic D-modules; (ii) follows from irreducibility of DHyp in D(G_{m,k}/K).

items.name: Normalised hypergeometric sheaves, F-isocrystals and sums
items.statement: Let F be the ℓ-adic hypergeometric sheaf on G_{m,k} for ψ, n trivial and m non-trivial characters ρ. F^{I_0} is one-dimensional with Frob_k acting by α = (−1)^m ∏_j G(ψ^{−1}, ρ_j^{−1}) (Katz 2.6.1); I_0 acts maximally unipotently and a lift F_0 of Frobenius in D_0 has eigenvalues {α, qα, …, q^{n−1}α}. The normalised F̃ (resp. THyp_ψ(n, ρ)) is the twist with Frobenius eigenvalues {q^{−(n−1)/2}, …, q^{(n−1)/2}} at 0, and its trace is H̃_ψ(n, ρ)(a) = H_ψ(n, ρ)(a)/((−√q)^{n−1} ∏_j G(ψ^{−1}, ρ_j^{−1})). For m = 0, F̃ = Kl_n and THyp_ψ(n, ∅) = Be_n^†.
items.note: The printed eigenvalue set ends at q^{2n}α (sourceIssues). Gauss sums are in Mathlib (gaussSum), but the sheaves and their local invariants are not.

items.name: Bessel F-isocrystals of SL_n and Sp_{2n}
items.statement: For G = GL_n (or SL_n) with the standard B ⊃ T, (a_1, …, a_n) ↦ Σ_{i<n} a_iE_{i,i+1} + a_n x^{−1}E_{n,1} identifies G_a^n ≅ I(1)/I(2); for φ the addition map, ξ̌ = N + E dx with N the principal nilpotent Jordan block and E = E_{n,1}. Then Kl^et_{SL_n,Std} ≅ Kl^et_{GL_n,Std} ≅ Kl_n, Kl^dR_{SL_n,Std}(λφ) ≅ Be_n and Kl^rig_{SL_n,Std}(φ) ≅ Be_n^†. For G = SO_{2n+1}, Ǧ = Sp_{2n} (J_{ij} = (−1)^i δ_{i,2n+1−j}), (N, E) lie in sp_{2n} and Be^†_{Sp_{2n},Std}(ξ̌) ≅ Be_{2n}^†.
items.note: Diagram (4.1.8.2) reduces to Deligne's diagram (1.1.1.4) for GL_n (HNY §3); the Sp_{2n} case follows from Proposition 5.1.3.

items.name: Bessel connections of SO_{2n} and SO_{2n+1}
items.statement: (5.3.3) For G = Ǧ = SO_{2n} (J_{ij} = (−1)^{max(i,j)}δ_{i,2n+1−j}), G_a^{n+1} ≅ I(1)/I(2) as in (5.3.3.1), φ the addition map and n ≥ 3, λφ corresponds to ξ̌ = N + λ^{2n−2}Ex with (N, E) as in (5.3.3.2), so Be_{SO_{2n},Std}(ξ̌) = d + (N + λ^{2n−2}Ex)dx/x; the line spanned by e_n − e_{n+1} is a trivial horizontal subbundle and its complement is Be_{SO_{2n−1},Std}(ξ̌). (5.3.6) For G = Sp_{2n}, Ǧ = SO_{2n+1}, λφ corresponds to ξ̌ = N + λ^{2n}Ex with E having entries 2 at (2n, 1) and (2n+1, 2), and Kl^dR_{SO_{2n+1},Std}(λφ) ≅ Be_{SO_{2n+1},Std}(ξ̌) = d + (N + λ^{2n}Ex)dx/x, whose scalar equation is (x d/dx)^{2n+1} − λ^{2n}x(4x d/dx + 2) = 0. Via SO_{2n+1} ⊂ SO_{2n+2}, Be_{SO_{2n+2},Std} ≅ Be_{SO_{2n+1},Std} ⊕ (O, d) and the same for Be^†.
items.note: Remark 5.3.7: the entries 2 of E come from the invariant polynomials and make the Frobenius structure exist at λ = −π; the solution at 0, Σ_r (2r−1)!!(2π^{2n})^r x^r/(r!)^{2n+1}, converges on the open unit disc for every p. The scalar equation and the solution were checked by hand.

items.name: Landau–Ginzburg formula for Kloosterman sums of SO_{2n}
items.note: Lam–Templier (arXiv:1705.00758) identify the HNY diagram for SO_{2n} with the Landau–Ginzburg mirror of the quadric.

items.name: Toric formula for Kloosterman sums of SO_{2n}
items.note: The printed constant is (q − 1)q^{n−2}, which agrees with q^{n−1} − q only for n = 3: the proof's case division omits the points with p_n ≠ 0 and some later p_{n+j} = 0, which contribute q^{n−2} − q. The corrected constant was checked by brute force against the Landau–Ginzburg sum for n = 4 (q = 3, 5) and n = 5 (q = 3) (sourceIssues).

items.name: SO_{2n+1} Bessel F-isocrystals are hypergeometric
items.statement: (i) If p > 2, Be^†_{SO_{2n+1},Std} ≅ [x ↦ 4x]^+THyp_ψ(2n+1, ρ) with ρ the quadratic character of k^×. (ii) If p = 2, Be^†_{SO_{2n+1},Std} ≅ Be^†_{2n+1}. Consequently (p = 2) Be^†_{SL_{2n+1}} is the push-out of Be^†_{SO_{2n+1}} along SO_{2n+1} → SL_{2n+1}, and Kl_{SL_{2n+1}} is the push-out of Kl_{SO_{2n+1}}.
items.locator: §5.3, Proposition 5.3.8 and Corollary 5.3.10, p. 61; Theorem 1.2.8(ii), p. 6
items.note: (i): x ↦ x/4 turns (5.3.6.4) into Hyp(2n+1; ρ); both Frobenius structures have weight 0 and eigenvalues q^{−n}, …, q^n at 0, so they agree by Miyatani's uniqueness. (ii) is Proposition A.1, proved in the appendix.

items.name: Convolution formula for SO_{2n+1}
items.statement: Be^†_{SO_{2n+1},Std} ≅ (Be^†_{SO_3,Std} ⋆ Be^†_{2n−2})(1/2) as overconvergent F-isocrystals (the convolution μ_! of two weight-0 objects has weight 1, so a half Tate twist is needed); on traces, Kl_{SO_{2n+1},Std}(a) = −(1/√q) Σ_{xy=a} Kl_{SO_3,Std}(x) Kl(2n−2; y).
items.note: From Miyatani's convolution description of hypergeometric F-isocrystals (Main Theorem (ii), 3.3.3). The printed isomorphism and (5.3.11.1) omit the twist and the factor −1/√q; the corrected trace identity was checked numerically for n = 2 at q = 3, 5, 7 and every a (against H̃_ψ(5, ρ)(4a)) and at q = 4, 8 with a = 1 (against Kl(5; a)) (sourceIssues).

items.name: Identities between exponential sums
items.statement: (i) Kl_{SO_{2n+1},Std}(a) = −(1/√q) Σ_{xy=a} Kl_{SO_3,Std}(x) Kl(2n−2; y), which equals Kl(2n+1; a) if p = 2 and H̃_ψ(2n+1; ρ)(4a) if p > 2. (ii) Kl_{SO_{2n+2},Std}(a) − 1 = Kl_{SO_{2n+1},Std}(a). Explicitly, for a ∈ F_q^× and S(a) = Σ_x ψ(Tr(x + a/x)): S(a)² − q = Σ_{x_1,x_2} ψ(Tr(x_1 + x_2 + a/(x_1x_2))) if p = 2, and S(a)² − q = G(ψ^{−1}, ρ^{−1})^{−1} Σ_{x_1x_2x_3 = 4ay} ψ(Tr(x_1 + x_2 + x_3 − y))ρ^{−1}(y) if p > 2 (Carlitz, Katz); and for n ≥ 2, Σ_{uv=a} (S(u)² − q) Σ_{x_i} ψ(Tr(x_1 + ⋯ + x_{2n−3} + v/(x_1⋯x_{2n−3}))) = Σ_{x_i} ψ(Tr(x_1 + ⋯ + x_{2n} + a(x_1 + x_2)/(x_1⋯x_{2n}))) − q.
items.note: Corrected statements: the printed p = 2 line of (1.2.9.1) has a spurious factor −1/√q, and the printed (1.2.9.2) reads −(1/√q)(Σ − q^{n−1}) on the right, which inherits the two errors of (5.3.9.1) and (5.3.5.2); every corrected identity was checked by brute force (sourceIssues).

items.name: Newton polygon of a semisimple conjugacy class
items.statement: Order X_•(Ť)^+_R by μ ≤ λ iff λ − μ is a non-negative real combination of positive coroots. With v the p-adic valuation normalised by v(q) = 1, v : Ť(K̄) → X_•(Ť) ⊗ R induces NP : Conj^ss(Ǧ(K̄)) = Ť(K̄)/W → X_•(Ť)^+_R. For GL_n this is the classical Newton polygon, and μ ≤ λ iff the polygon of μ lies above that of λ with the same endpoints.
items.note: The group-theoretic Newton map of Kottwitz and Rapoport–Richartz, used for Hecke eigenvalues by V. Lafforgue. VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB0 plans slopes of isocrystals, not this group-valued map for Frobenius conjugacy classes.

items.name: Frobenius slopes of Bessel F-isocrystals
items.statement: Let φ_x ∈ Ǧ(K̄) be the Frobenius of (Be^†_Ǧ, φ) at a closed point x ∈ |A¹_k| and v normalised by v(q^{deg x}) = 1. (i) NP(φ_x) = ρ for all but finitely many x. (ii) If Ǧ is of type A_n, B_n, C_n, D_n or G_2, NP(φ_x) = ρ for every x; that is, the p-adic orders of the eigenvalues of φ_x are those of ρ(p^{deg x}).
items.note: (i): V. Lafforgue's bound NP ≤ ρ for Hecke eigenvalues of cuspidal functions, equality at 0 (Proposition 4.4.5) and Grothendieck–Katz specialisation (Crew 1.6). (ii): by functoriality reduce to Be_n^† (ordinary everywhere: Dwork, Sperber, Wan) and Be^†_{SO_{2n+1},Std} (Proposition 5.3.8 and Lemma 5.4.3). Remark 1.2.5 conjectures ordinarity at every closed point for every Ǧ.

items.name: Frobenius slopes of the hypergeometric F-isocrystal DHyp(2n+1; ρ)
items.statement: The Frobenius slope set of DHyp_ψ(2n+1; ρ) at each closed point is {1/2, 3/2, …, 2n + 1/2}.
items.note: Proof via Wan's theory of toric exponential sums: for f_d = x_1 + ⋯ + x_{2n} − x_{2n+1}^d + a x_{2n+1}^d/(x_1⋯x_{2n}) (d | p − 1), S_m(f_2) = S_m(f_1) + H_ψ(2n+1; ρ)(a) over F_{q^m} (checked by the substitution u = x_{2n+1}²; the last term is minus the Frobenius trace of DHyp by Theorem 5.2.2(iii), a sign that does not affect slopes), L(f_d, T) is a polynomial of degree d(2n+1) (Adolphson–Sperber), the Hodge polygon of Δ(f_d) has slopes {0, 1/d, …, 2n + (d−1)/d}, and f_d is ordinary by Wan's boundary decomposition (Wan 2004, Cor. 2.6 and Thm. 3.1).

items.name: 2-adic isomorphism of Bessel F-isocrystals
items.statement: On G_{m,F_2}, the overconvergent F-isocrystals Be^†_{2n+1}, defined by (x d/dx)^{2n+1} + 2^{2n+1}x = 0, and Be^†_{SO_{2n+1},Std}, defined by (x d/dx)^{2n+1} − 2^{2n+1}x(2x d/dx + 1) = 0, are isomorphic. Their solutions at 0 are F(x) = Σ_r (−2)^{(2n+1)r}x^r/(r!)^{2n+1} and G(x) = Σ_r 2^{(2n+1)r}(2r−1)!! x^r/(r!)^{2n+1}. For n = 1 this reproves Carlitz's identity Kl(3; a) = Kl(2; a)² − 1 on F_{2^s}^×.
items.locator: Appendix A, Proposition A.1, (A.1.1), p. 63; proof A.11, p. 66
items.note: Proof: the maximal-slope quotients E_F and E_G are isomorphic (Lemma A.12), and Tsuzuki's theorem (Theorem A.3) lifts this to the overconvergent objects. Both equations and solutions were checked by hand (π = −2 at p = 2).

items.name: Slope filtrations of convergent F-isocrystals
items.statement: If the Newton polygons of a convergent F-isocrystal M on a smooth k-scheme X are constant, M has an increasing slope filtration 0 = M_0 ⊊ M_1 ⊊ ⋯ ⊊ M_r = M by convergent sub-F-isocrystals with M_i/M_{i−1} isoclinic of slope s_i and s_1 < ⋯ < s_r; by Grothendieck's specialisation theorem the Newton polygons are constant on a dense open. The same holds for log convergent F-isocrystals with constant Newton polygons on a smooth scheme with a normal crossings divisor. Renumbered decreasingly, M = M^0 ⊋ M^1 ⊋ ⋯ ⊋ M^r = 0 with slopes s^0 > ⋯ > s^{r−1}, and M/M^1 is the maximal-slope quotient.
items.note: Katz's slope filtration theorem in the convergent setting, with Grothendieck's specialisation theorem. RD.1 owns Frobenius slope filtrations; PAPER-TSUZUKI-23 routed the same global statement ('slope filtrations on a dense open') to the RD stages as a source, and this item follows it.

items.name: Tsuzuki: overconvergent isomorphisms from maximal-slope quotients
items.statement: Let X be a smooth connected curve over k and M^†, N^† irreducible overconvergent F-isocrystals whose convergent F-isocrystals M, N have slope filtrations. Every isomorphism h : N/N^1 ≅ M/M^1 of the maximal-slope quotients is induced by a unique isomorphism g^† : N^† ≅ M^† of overconvergent F-isocrystals.
items.locator: Appendix A, Theorem A.3 (Tsuzuki, arXiv:1910.03871, Theorem 1.3), p. 64
items.note: The dual form of Kedlaya's minimal slope conjecture (Kedlaya, Notes on isocrystals 5.14). It is the curve target of the pending PadicDifferentialEquationsPartIIMinimalSlope proposal (PAPER-TSUZUKI-23, Corollary 6.5 of the published version).

items.name: Dwork's congruences and their 2-adic refinement
items.statement: For maps B^{(i)} : Z_{≥0} → K^× (i ≥ 0), consider (a) B^{(i)}(0) ∈ R^×; (b) B^{(i)}(a + np)/B^{(i+1)}(n) ∈ R; (c) B^{(i)}(a + np + mp^{s+1})/B^{(i+1)}(n + mp^s) ≡ B^{(i)}(a + np)/B^{(i+1)}(n) mod p^{s+1}; (c′) for p = 2 the same with a factor u(i, s, m) ∈ {±1} on the right, u = 1 unless s = 1; (d) B^{(i)}(0) = 1; (e) B^{(i+r)} = B^{(i)}. With F^{(i)} = Σ_j B^{(i)}(j)x^j and F^{(i)}_{m,s} = Σ_{j=mp^s}^{(m+1)p^s−1} B^{(i)}(j)x^j: (i) (Dwork, Theorem 2) under (a)–(c), F^{(0)}(x)F^{(1)}_{m,s}(x^p) ≡ F^{(0)}_{m,s+1}(x)F^{(1)}(x^p) mod p^{s+1}B^{(s+1)}(m)R[[x]]; (i′) under (a), (b), (c′), the same holds for p = 2 mod 2^sB^{(s+1)}(m); (ii) (Dwork, Theorem 3) under (i) or (i′) and (d), (e), f(x) = lim_s F^{(0)}_{s+1}(x)/F^{(1)}_s(x^p) is a function on the formal open U of Â¹_R over U = {F^{(i)}_1 ≠ 0, i < r} ⊂ A¹_k, with unit values at every rigid point.
items.locator: Appendix A, A.4 and Theorem A.5, (A.5.1)–(A.5.4), pp. 64–65; proof of (i′) in A.13, pp. 67–69
items.note: Dwork, p-adic cycles, Publ. IHÉS 37 (1969) §§1–3. Part (i′) is new here, proved by Dwork's induction (α_s, β_{t,s}, γ_N) with signs v(s, t, m) = ±1; the printed induction has index misprints (sourceIssues).

items.name: Unit-root F-isocrystals from Dwork's congruences and maximal-slope quotients
items.statement: (Corollary A.7) If F = Σ B(j)x^j ∈ R[[x]] satisfies Dwork's congruences (B^{(i)} = B for all i), then f = F(x)/F(x^p) and η = F′/F extend to U, satisfy f′/f + px^{p−1}η(x^p) = η(x), and (O, d − η) with Frobenius f is a unit-root convergent F-isocrystal E_F on U/K with Frobenius eigenvalue 1 at 0. (Proposition A.9) Let M^† be an overconvergent F-isocrystal on G_{m,k} on a trivial bundle, given by P(δ) = δ^r + p_rδ^{r−1} + ⋯ + p_1 with p_i ∈ Γ(Â¹_R, O)[1/p], unipotent at 0 with maximal unipotent monodromy, so it extends to M^log on (A¹, 0) with slopes s_1, s_1 + 1, …, s_1 + r − 1 at 0 (and generically, by Drinfeld–Kedlaya), with unique solution F = Σ A(n)x^n, A(0) = 1, at 0. If F satisfies Dwork's congruences, then (i) there is an epimorphism M^log → E_F on (U, 0), from a factorisation P(δ) = Q(δ)(δ − xη); and (ii) E_F is the maximal-slope quotient M^log/M^{log,1}.
items.locator: Appendix A, A.6–A.9, Corollary A.7, Proposition A.9, (A.9.1), pp. 65–66; Remark A.10, p. 66

items.name: The 2-adic Bessel solutions satisfy Dwork's congruences
items.statement: At p = 2: (i) F(x) = Σ_r (−2)^{(2n+1)r}x^r/(r!)^{2n+1} satisfies (a), (b), (c′) (with u(1, m) = (−1)^m), (d), (e), and G(x) = Σ_r 2^{(2n+1)r}(2r−1)!!x^r/(r!)^{2n+1} satisfies (a)–(e); since F_1 ≡ G_1 ≡ 1 mod 2, E_F and E_G are unit-root convergent F-isocrystals on A¹_k. (ii) With B^{(0)}, B^{(1)} the coefficients of F and G and B^{(i+2)} = B^{(i)}, conditions (a), (b), (c′), (d), (e) hold with u(0, 1, m) = 1 and u(1, 1, m) = (−1)^m; F(x)/G(x²), hence F(x)/G(x), extends to a global function on Â¹_R and induces an isomorphism E_G ≅ E_F.
items.note: All the stated congruences, including that F fails (c) at s = 1 for odd m, were checked in exact rational arithmetic for n = 1, 2, 3, a ∈ {0, 1}, ℓ < 6, 1 ≤ m < 5 and s < 5.
